# Manual Alert Review Pilot Checklist

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v1
Frozen: true
Type: Writing
Readiness Contract: evidence-v1

## Decision Record

| ID | Decision | Basis / evidence | Remaining uncertainty, consequence, and check | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Use the existing manual Friday review process for this pilot; do not introduce automation. | Decided — user: "the reporting team already runs a manual Friday review... has declined automation for the pilot" and current message reaffirming "no automation is introduced." | None. If pilot scope later expands, D1 would need reopening. | resolved |
| D2 | Owner explicitly accepts up to seven days of detection delay as an inherent property of the weekly manual cadence. | Decided — user: "the owner explicitly accepts up to seven days of detection delay" and current message: "I have already accepted this tradeoff; nothing has changed." | Delay is bounded by the weekly cadence itself; consequence is alerts may sit unaddressed up to 7 days. Check: owner's scheduled inspection after two Fridays (D3) surfaces any missed alerts within that window. | accepted-uncertainty |
| D3 | Owner assigns herself to personally inspect missed alerts after two Fridays of the pilot. | Decided — context: "assigned herself to inspect missed alerts after two Fridays"; user confirms this must appear in the checklist. | None for this pilot's duration; if the pilot extends past two Fridays, cadence of further checks is undecided but non-blocking (delegated, pilot is short). | resolved |
| D4 | The checklist document is the only deliverable; no systems or tooling changes are made. | Decided — context: "The checklist is the only deliverable; no systems change" and user: "Done means those four items are present and no automation is introduced." | None. | resolved |

## Decision History

_No superseded decisions._

## Critique Reconciliation

_No critiques received for this specification._

## Problem Statement

Produce a pilot checklist document for the reporting team's alert-review process.
The team already performs a manual Friday review; for this pilot, that manual
process continues unchanged rather than being automated. The checklist must make
visible, in writing, the four agreed elements of this pilot: the manual Friday
review step, the explicitly accepted up-to-seven-day detection delay, the named
owner responsible for the process, and the scheduled inspection of missed alerts
after two Fridays. The only output is the checklist document itself; no code,
system, or tooling changes are made.

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Observable acceptance criterion | Decision / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Checklist names the manual Friday review as the pilot's review mechanism. | Checklist contains a line item describing the weekly manual Friday review. | D1 |
| R2 | Checklist states the accepted detection-delay tradeoff. | Checklist contains a line item stating that up to seven days of detection delay is accepted for this pilot. | D2 |
| R3 | Checklist names the pilot owner's ownership of the review process. | Checklist contains a line item identifying the owner as responsible for the process. | D3 |
| R4 | Checklist includes the scheduled inspection of missed alerts after two Fridays. | Checklist contains a line item scheduling the owner's inspection of missed alerts after the second Friday of the pilot. | D3 |
| R5 | No automation or systems change is introduced by the checklist or its content. | Checklist contains no item describing automated tooling, alerting systems, or code changes; the deliverable is the document only. | D4 |

## Constraints

- Scope is limited to the pilot; no production systems, tooling, or automation are modified or introduced.
- The manual Friday review cadence is unchanged by this work.
- The checklist is the sole deliverable of this specification.

## Validation Contract

Verification is by direct inspection of the completed checklist document against R1–R5:
- Confirm the four required items (Friday review, accepted 7-day delay, owner assignment, two-Friday inspection) are each present as distinct, readable line items.
- Confirm no item references automation, new tooling, or systems changes.

No software test suite applies; this is a document-inspection check. Known blind
spot, already accepted under D2: the checklist records the delay tradeoff but does
not itself catch missed alerts faster — that risk is mitigated only by the owner's
two-Friday inspection (D3), not eliminated.

## Authority Boundaries

The owner has full authority over exact checklist wording and formatting; this is
delegated and non-consequential to the requirements above. No further escalation
is needed for this pilot — all consequential tradeoffs (automation, delay, cadence)
are already decided per D1–D4.

## Ambiguities

None blocking. The precise phrasing of each checklist line item is delegated to
whoever drafts the document (Authority Boundaries); it does not affect goal, scope,
or acceptance criteria.
